title: Risk and Honest Interval Length for Gaussian Dose-Policy Values from Noisy-Dose Records
banked_reason: Math review passed; D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field, paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4, salvageable=false; independent validity gate confirms no bounded same-topic repair.
gap_reasons: The oscillator proof, deterministic bias control, and legal original-record testing alternatives establish the matched risk and honest-length orders on the stipulated class; no stale matched-frontier overclaim remains. The contribution is an explicit Gaussian-width evaluation, rather than a general inversion framework beyond the credited [Hermite constructions](https://arxiv.org/html/1112.4565v4) and [functional duality theorem](https://people.lids.mit.edu/yp/homepage/data/dual2.pdf). Its econometric reach is confined to randomized Gaussian doses, a known Gaussian channel, and the specified binary response envelope. The practical promise of choosing widths permitting informative intervals is under-delivered by the supplied procedure: at n=1,000,000, its endpoint bias certificates alone are approximately 597 and 454, against a target range of length 0.5. Universal rate comparisons therefore establish asymptotic precision orders without delivering useful finite-sample planning calibration, and no numerical implementation demonstrates an informative alternative. These scope and operational limitations constrain the projected paper score even after competent rewriting. tldr: The Gaussian variance-policy frontier is evaluated on one fixed bounded-Lipschitz Bernoulli response class from the original noisy-dose records. For all \(n\ge3\) and \(v\in[1/4,7/4]\), the finite cutoff \(J_n^{\mathrm{audit}}=\max\{j:n^2r^{4j}\ge j+1\}\) and the finite sum \(\rho(n,v)=d_v^2(\lambda_0n)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{J_n^{\mathrm{audit}}}a_jz(v)^j\) give \(R(n,v)\asymp\rho(n,v)\) and \(L_{90}(n,v)\asymp\sqrt{\rho(n,v)}\), with universal constants. Total original-record procedures attain these orders and provide finite-sample coverage at least \(0.90\). Fixed interior variances \(1/2<v<3/2\) have risk order \(n^{-1}\); both endpoints have risk order \(\sqrt{\log n}/n\) and honest-length order \((\log n)^{1/4}/\sqrt n\). At a fixed exterior variance, \(\beta(v)=\log(1/|q(v)|)/\log(1/r)\) gives risk order \(n^{-\beta(v)}(\log n)^{\beta(v)/2-1}\) and length order \(n^{-\beta(v)/2}(\log n)^{\beta(v)/4-1/2}\). The finite expression retains every crossover, with critical windows of width order \(1/\log n\). For \(v^\dagger=3/(4v)\) within the policy domain, \(z(v^\dagger)=z(v)\), \(\rho(n,v^\dagger)=\alpha v\rho(n,v)\), and \(\ell(n,v^\dagger)=\sqrt{\alpha v}\ell(n,v)\); in particular \(1/2\) and \(3/2\) are paired. These are exact proxy identities, transferred to risk and length only by universal comparisons. The result is a prospective precision benchmark, with no production implementation, priority claim, or exact minimax constant claim.
gap: General linear-functional deconvolution and inverse-information theory do not by themselves evaluate the linked Gaussian response envelope as the centered policy variance crosses both square-integrability boundaries. Generic functional duality already characterizes risk through a modulus, so another unevaluated modulus would not close this gap.
fill: Even bounded Gaussian-weighted Hermite functions expose the actual marked-law quadratic form. The finite sum \(\mathcal S_M(v)\), uniform certificate \(\varepsilon_M(v)\), and scalar audit root \(x_n\) specify an auditable starting calculation; a finite certified index bounds absolute target error by \(1/(100n)\). The explicit norm-scaled witness supplies same-class alternatives with bounded product divergence. All-order coefficient and derivative control determine the sharp evaluation through the lower smoothing boundary and upper tail-integrability boundary.
